questions.question: What is a life cycle, and why do we draw it as a circle?
questions.expected_answer: A life cycle shows the stages a living thing goes through, from seed or egg to adult. We draw it as a circle because the adult reproduces and makes young, which grow into adults that reproduce again, so the last stage leads back to the first.

questions.question: Describe the life cycle of a maize plant.
questions.expected_answer: A seed germinates in warm, damp soil and grows a root and shoot. It becomes a seedling, then an adult plant. The plant makes flowers: a tassel with pollen and silk on the young cobs. The wind pollinates the silk, and new seeds, the kernels, form on the cob. These seeds can be planted to start again.

questions.question: Describe the life cycle of the mopane emperor moth, and explain why it is called metamorphosis.
questions.expected_answer: The female moth lays eggs on a mopane tree. They hatch into caterpillars, the mopane worms, which eat leaves and grow. A fully grown caterpillar burrows into the soil and becomes a pupa. An adult moth comes out, mates and lays eggs. It is metamorphosis because the body changes shape completely.
